words.defn_en: confused or bewildered:

sentences.en: He gave a ______ look when asked to explain the missing funds.
sentences.zh: 被問及那筆不見的資金時,他露出一臉困惑的表情。

sentences.en: The ______ tourist wandered the station for an hour before finding the right platform.
sentences.zh: 這名迷糊的遊客在車站徘徊了一個小時,才找到正確的月台。

words.defn_en: to make dirty or grimy:

sentences.en: Years of factory smoke had begun to ______ the once-white building facade.
sentences.zh: 多年的工廠煙塵,讓這棟原本潔白的建築外牆逐漸沾滿汙垢。

sentences.en: The miners emerged from the tunnel, their faces thoroughly ______d with coal dust.
sentences.zh: 礦工們從隧道裡出來時,臉上滿是煤塵。

words.defn_en: to be resentful or reluctant:

sentences.en: I don't ______ him his success; he worked hard for it.
sentences.zh: 我並不嫉妒他的成功,那是他努力得來的。

sentences.en: She ______d every penny spent on her sister's lavish wedding.
sentences.zh: 她對花在姊姊那場奢華婚禮上的每一分錢都感到不甘心。

words.defn_en: to trick, deceive:

sentences.en: The con artist managed to ______ several elderly victims out of their savings.
sentences.zh: 這名騙子成功欺騙了好幾位年長的受害者,騙走了他們的積蓄。

sentences.en: Her charming smile ______d everyone at the party.
sentences.zh: 她迷人的微笑迷惑了派對上的每一個人。

words.defn_en: charmed or enchanted, often in a deceptive way:

sentences.en: The investors, ______ by his confident promises, handed over their savings.
sentences.zh: 投資人被他信心滿滿的承諾迷惑,把積蓄都交了出去。

sentences.en: She remained ______ by the con man's charm even after the warning signs appeared.
sentences.zh: 即使警訊已經出現,她仍被這名騙子的魅力迷得神魂顛倒。

words.defn_en: charming or attractive in a deceptive way:
words.defn_zh: 迷人的;誘人的(帶有欺騙性)

sentences.en: The ad's ______ promises turned out to be too good to be true.
sentences.zh: 這則廣告誘人的承諾,結果證明好得令人難以置信。

sentences.en: There was something ______ about the stranger's smile that made her lower her guard.
sentences.zh: 那名陌生人笑容中有種迷人的東西,讓她放下了戒心。

words.defn_en: to cut off the head of someone:

sentences.en: The deposed king was publicly ______ed before a large crowd.
sentences.zh: 這位被廢黜的國王在眾目睽睽之下被公開斬首。

sentences.en: Historical records describe how the executioner would ______ prisoners with a single stroke.
sentences.zh: 史料記載,劊子手會一刀就將囚犯斬首。

words.defn_en: something of tremendous power or size:

sentences.en: The new shopping mall is a ______ that dwarfs every other building downtown.
sentences.zh: 這座新購物中心是個龐然大物,讓市中心其他建築都相形見絀。

sentences.en: The company grew from a small startup into a corporate ______.
sentences.zh: 這家公司從一間小型新創企業成長為企業界的龐然大物。

words.defn_en: late, delayed:

sentences.en: He sent a ______ birthday card two weeks after her birthday.
sentences.zh: 他在她生日過後兩週才寄出遲來的生日卡。

sentences.en: The company issued a ______ apology for the data breach.
sentences.zh: 這家公司對這起資料外洩事件發表了一份遲來的道歉聲明。

words.defn_en: to give a false impression of; to contradict:

sentences.en: Her calm expression ______ the panic she felt inside.
sentences.zh: 她鎮定的表情掩飾了內心的恐慌。

sentences.en: The building's plain exterior ______ the luxury hidden within.
sentences.zh: 這棟建築樸素的外觀,與內部隱藏的奢華形成矛盾。

words.defn_en: to make seem less important:

sentences.en: She always tries to ______ her coworkers' achievements in meetings.
sentences.zh: 她總是在會議中試圖貶低同事的成就。

sentences.en: Parents should never ______ their children's efforts, even when they fail.
sentences.zh: 即使孩子失敗了,父母也絕不該貶低他們的努力。

words.defn_en: making someone or something seem unimportant:

sentences.en: His ______ comments about her work left her feeling discouraged.
sentences.zh: 他對她作品貶低的評論,讓她感到十分氣餒。

sentences.en: Constant ______ from a supervisor can quickly destroy an employee's confidence.
sentences.zh: 上司持續的貶低,能很快摧毀員工的信心。

words.defn_en: of a quarrelsome nature; eager to fight; warlike; belligerent

sentences.en: The dictator's ______ rhetoric alarmed neighboring countries.
sentences.zh: 這位獨裁者好戰的言論讓鄰國感到不安。

sentences.en: His ______ attitude made peace talks nearly impossible.
sentences.zh: 他好戰的態度讓和平談判幾乎不可能進行。

words.defn_en: warlike:

sentences.en: The ______ nation refused every offer of peace talks.
sentences.zh: 這個好戰的國家拒絕了每一次和談的提議。

sentences.en: He became ______ after just a few drinks at the party.
sentences.zh: 他在派對上才喝了幾杯酒就變得好鬥起來。

words.defn_en: something that indicates a future trend; a leader:

sentences.en: Economists watch housing starts as a ______ for the broader economy.
sentences.zh: 經濟學家將新屋開工率視為判斷整體經濟的風向指標。

sentences.en: The small swing state has long served as a political ______ in national elections.
sentences.zh: 這個規模不大的搖擺州,長久以來一直是全國選舉的政治風向球。

words.defn_en: to express regret or dissatisfaction about something:

sentences.en: Fans continued to ______ the team's decision to trade their star player.
sentences.zh: 球迷們持續哀嘆球隊交易掉明星球員的決定。

sentences.en: He spent the whole dinner ______ing his bad luck at the casino.
sentences.zh: 他整頓晚餐都在哀嘆自己在賭場的壞運氣。

words.defn_en: to puzzle or confuse someone, often mildly:

sentences.en: The abstract painting seemed to ______ more visitors than it inspired.
sentences.zh: 這幅抽象畫似乎讓更多參觀者感到困惑,而非受到啟發。

sentences.en: Her unusual choice of words tended to ______ non-native speakers.
sentences.zh: 她用詞獨特的方式,常讓非母語人士感到一頭霧水。

words.defn_en: charitable, kindly:

sentences.en: The ______ donor gave millions to build the new children's hospital.
sentences.zh: 這位仁慈的捐贈者捐出數百萬元興建這座新的兒童醫院。

sentences.en: The old king was remembered as a wise and ______ ruler.
sentences.zh: 這位老國王被人們記得是一位睿智又仁慈的統治者。

words.defn_en: lacking cultural or moral enlightenment; ignorant:

sentences.en: The reformer worked to bring education to what he called the ______ countryside.
sentences.zh: 這位改革者致力於為他口中「愚昧」的鄉村地區帶來教育。

sentences.en: Later generations often view earlier eras as ______ , forgetting their own future critics.
sentences.zh: 後代常視前人的時代為愚昧無知,卻忘了自己也終將被後人如此評價。

words.defn_en: to make numb, physically or emotionally:

sentences.en: The freezing wind began to ______ his fingers within minutes.
sentences.zh: 凜冽的寒風幾分鐘內就讓他的手指變得麻木。

sentences.en: Years of repeated tragedy had begun to ______ the community's capacity for grief.
sentences.zh: 多年反覆發生的悲劇,讓這個社群感受悲傷的能力逐漸麻木。

words.defn_en: to pass on, give:

sentences.en: Her grandfather chose to ______ his entire library to the local school.
sentences.zh: 她的祖父選擇將他全部的藏書遺贈給當地的學校。

sentences.en: The old king would ______ his throne to his eldest daughter.
sentences.zh: 這位老國王將把王位傳給他的長女。

words.defn_en: to rebuke or scold in a harsh tone

sentences.en: The coach began to ______ the team for their careless mistakes.
sentences.zh: 教練開始嚴厲斥責球隊犯下的粗心錯誤。

sentences.en: She hated being ______d in front of her coworkers.
sentences.zh: 她很討厭在同事面前被嚴厲責罵。

words.defn_en: to deprive someone of a loved one, especially through death:

sentences.en: The sudden accident would ______ the family of their eldest son.
sentences.zh: 這場突如其來的意外,將奪走這個家庭的長子。

sentences.en: War tends to ______ entire generations of fathers, brothers, and sons.
sentences.zh: 戰爭往往讓整個世代都喪失了父親、兄弟與兒子。

words.defn_en: having recently lost a loved one through death:

sentences.en: The support group offers counseling to ______ families free of charge.
sentences.zh: 這個支持團體為喪親家庭提供免費諮商。

sentences.en: Neighbors brought meals to the ______ widow every day for a month.
sentences.zh: 鄰居們連續一個月,每天都為這位喪偶的寡婦送餐。

words.defn_en: state of sorrow over the death or departure of a loved one:

sentences.en: The company offers employees a week of ______ leave after losing a family member.
sentences.zh: 公司在員工失去家人後,提供一週的喪假。

sentences.en: The support group helps people cope with the pain of ______.
sentences.zh: 這個互助團體幫助人們應對喪親之痛。

words.defn_en: deprived of:

sentences.en: After the loss of her husband, she felt utterly ______.
sentences.zh: 在失去丈夫之後,她感到徹底的孤苦無依。

sentences.en: The village was left ______ of resources after the flood.
sentences.zh: 洪水過後,這座村莊喪失了一切資源。

words.defn_en: to beg, plead, implore:

sentences.en: She fell to her knees to ______ the judge for mercy.
sentences.zh: 她跪下懇求法官網開一面。

sentences.en: The villagers began to ______ the king to lower their taxes.
sentences.zh: 村民們開始懇求國王降低他們的稅賦。

words.defn_en: to trouble or harass persistently:

sentences.en: The project was ______ by delays and budget overruns from the very start.
sentences.zh: 這項計畫從一開始就飽受延誤與預算超支的困擾。

sentences.en: Doubts continued to ______ her even after the decision was final.
sentences.zh: 即使決定已成定局,疑慮仍持續困擾著她。

words.defn_en: to surround, hem in:

sentences.en: The ancient army chose to ______ the city rather than attack it directly.
sentences.zh: 這支古代軍隊選擇圍困這座城市,而非直接發動攻擊。

sentences.en: Reporters ______d the celebrity's house after news of the scandal broke.
sentences.zh: 醜聞消息傳出後,記者們把這位名人的住家團團圍住。

words.defn_en: to cover with slime; to defile or defame:

sentences.en: The tabloids seemed determined to ______ the actor's reputation with every new rumor.
sentences.zh: 小報似乎鐵了心,要用每一則新的謠言來玷污這位演員的名聲。

sentences.en: Rain had begun to ______ the muddy trail, making it treacherous to walk.
sentences.zh: 雨水已讓這條泥濘小徑變得又黏又滑,行走十分危險。

words.defn_en: to smear with saliva or drool; to fawn over excessively:

sentences.en: The puppy managed to ______ every pillow on the couch within minutes.
sentences.zh: 這隻小狗幾分鐘內就把沙發上的每個抱枕都弄得滿是口水。

sentences.en: Reviewers tend to ______ any film by a famous director, regardless of its quality.
sentences.zh: 評論家對知名導演的作品,常會不論品質好壞一味吹捧。

words.defn_en: to smear or stain, literally or figuratively:

sentences.en: The graffiti artist managed to ______ half the underpass in a single night.
sentences.zh: 這位塗鴉客一個晚上就把地下道的一半都畫滿了。

sentences.en: The campaign tried to ______ its opponent's reputation with unproven accusations.
sentences.zh: 這場競選活動試圖用未經證實的指控來玷污對手的名譽。

words.defn_en: to soil, stain, dim the reputation:

sentences.en: The scandal threatened to ______ his once spotless reputation.
sentences.zh: 這場醜聞可能會玷污他過去一塵不染的名聲。

sentences.en: She accused the tabloid of trying to ______ her career.
sentences.zh: 她指控這家八卦小報試圖詆毀她的事業。

words.defn_en: infatuated or obsessively fond of someone; intoxicated:

sentences.en: He was completely ______ with her from the moment they met.
sentences.zh: 從相遇的那一刻起,他就對她徹底著迷。

sentences.en: The ______ fans waited outside the stage door for hours.
sentences.zh: 這群為之著迷的粉絲在後台門口等了好幾個小時。

words.defn_en: to scatter something over a surface:

sentences.en: The baker likes to ______ powdered sugar over each finished pastry.
sentences.zh: 這位烘焙師喜歡在每個完成的糕點上撒些糖粉。

sentences.en: Morning dew seemed to ______ the entire meadow in tiny droplets.
sentences.zh: 清晨的露水彷彿為整片草原灑上了細小的水珠。

words.defn_en: savagely cruel; resembling an animal in behavior:

sentences.en: The soldiers carried out ______ acts against the defenseless villagers.
sentences.zh: 士兵們對手無寸鐵的村民犯下了殘暴的行徑。

sentences.en: The novel explores how war can reduce even civilized men to ______ behavior.
sentences.zh: 這部小說探討戰爭如何能讓文明人也淪為野蠻獸性的行為。

words.defn_en: to be cautious of possible danger:

sentences.en: The sign warned hikers to ______ of loose rocks on the trail.
sentences.zh: 告示牌警告健行者要留意步道上的鬆動落石。

sentences.en: Investors should ______ of any deal that promises guaranteed returns.
sentences.zh: 投資人應提防任何保證獲利的交易。

words.defn_en: to confuse someone greatly:

sentences.en: The maze of hallways continued to ______ new employees for weeks.
sentences.zh: 這座迷宮般的走廊,讓新進員工好幾個星期都摸不著頭緒。

sentences.en: The sudden change in the rules seemed designed to ______ the players.
sentences.zh: 規則的突然改變,似乎就是要讓玩家感到困惑。

words.defn_en: to cast a spell over; to captivate completely:

sentences.en: The dancer's grace seemed to ______ everyone in the audience.
sentences.zh: 這位舞者優雅的舞姿,彷彿讓在場觀眾都著了迷。

sentences.en: The old fairy tale tells of a witch who could ______ travelers who strayed off the path.
sentences.zh: 這則古老的童話講述一位女巫,能對誤入歧途的旅人施展魔法。

words.defn_en: prejudice:

sentences.en: The judge was accused of showing ______ toward one of the parties.
sentences.zh: 這名法官被指控對其中一方展現出偏見。

sentences.en: Researchers must be careful to avoid personal ______ when analyzing data.
sentences.zh: 研究人員在分析數據時必須小心避免個人偏見。

words.defn_en: showing unfair favoritism or prejudice:

sentences.en: Critics accused the study of being ______ toward the company that funded it.
sentences.zh: 評論家批評這項研究對出資的公司有失公允。

sentences.en: The referee's clearly ______ calls angered the visiting team's fans.
sentences.zh: 裁判明顯偏頗的判決,激怒了客隊球迷。

words.defn_en: a small, decorative object of little practical value:

sentences.en: Her mantelpiece was crowded with tiny porcelain ______ from her travels.
sentences.zh: 她的壁爐架上擺滿了旅行帶回的小瓷器擺飾。

sentences.en: The antique shop specialized in rare ______ rather than furniture.
sentences.zh: 這家古董店專門經營稀有的小古玩,而非家具。

words.defn_en: people who read too much and are intoxicated by books:
words.root_note: biblio- (book) + bibulus (fond of drinking), from Greek/Latin

sentences.en: The librarian jokingly called her regular patrons a happy tribe of ______.
sentences.zh: 這位圖書館員開玩笑地稱她的常客們是一群快樂的「書癡族」。

sentences.en: Coined by H. L. Mencken, the word ______ describes those who never seem to put a book down.
sentences.zh: 這個由孟肯所創造的字,用來形容那些手不釋卷、沉迷書本的人。

words.defn_en: a person who destroys or mutilates books:

sentences.en: The rare-book librarian shuddered at stories of a notorious ______ who tore pages for profit.
sentences.zh: 這位善本圖書館員一聽到某位惡名昭彰、撕書牟利的毀書者的故事就不寒而慄。

sentences.en: History remembers several regimes that acted as state-sponsored ______ , burning entire libraries.
sentences.zh: 史書記載,有些政權曾扮演國家級毀書者的角色,燒毀了整座圖書館。

words.defn_en: a list of sources used or referred to in a piece of writing:

sentences.en: The professor requires every essay to include a complete ______.
sentences.zh: 這位教授要求每篇論文都必須附上完整的參考書目。

sentences.en: Her ______ ran to twelve pages, reflecting years of careful research.
sentences.zh: 她的參考書目長達十二頁,反映出多年細緻的研究工作。

words.defn_en: a person who steals books:

sentences.en: The used bookstore installed cameras after several visits from a persistent ______.
sentences.zh: 這家二手書店在多次遭到慣竊書賊光顧後,安裝了監視攝影機。

sentences.en: Rare-book libraries take extra precautions to guard against the occasional ______.
sentences.zh: 善本圖書館採取額外的防範措施,以防偶爾出現的偷書賊。

words.defn_en: an extreme, often obsessive enthusiasm for collecting books:

sentences.en: His ______ had filled every room of the house with towering stacks of books.
sentences.zh: 他的藏書癖已讓屋裡每個房間都堆滿了高聳的書堆。

sentences.en: The auction attracted collectors whose ______ knew no budget limit.
sentences.zh: 這場拍賣會吸引了不論預算多高都要收藏的藏書狂熱者。

words.defn_en: a voracious reader; a devourer of books:

sentences.en: As a lifelong ______ , she finished nearly two hundred books a year.
sentences.zh: 身為終生嗜書如命的人,她每年幾乎讀完兩百本書。

sentences.en: The used bookstore was a paradise for any true ______.
sentences.zh: 這家二手書店對任何真正嗜書如命的人來說都是天堂。

words.defn_en: relating to a voracious devouring of books:

sentences.en: His ______ habits meant he carried at least three books in his bag at all times.
sentences.zh: 他嗜書如命的習慣,讓他隨時都在包裡帶著至少三本書。

sentences.en: The library's summer reading challenge rewards the most ______ students each year.
sentences.zh: 圖書館的暑期閱讀挑戰,每年都會獎勵讀書量最驚人的學生。

words.defn_en: a person who loves and collects books:

sentences.en: The estate sale drew ______ from three neighboring towns.
sentences.zh: 這場遺產拍賣吸引了鄰近三個城鎮的愛書人前來。

sentences.en: As a devoted ______ , she could never walk past a used bookstore without going in.
sentences.zh: 身為忠實的愛書人,她從不會經過二手書店而不進去逛逛。
